_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Fiji covering Lapita people settlement (~1500 BCE), Melanesian/Polynesian chiefdoms, cannibalism era ('Cannibal Isles'), European contact (Abel Tasman 1643, Cook 1774), Cakobau unification, cession to Britain 1874, indentured Indian labour (girmitiya 1879-1916), independence 1970, coups (1987 Rabuka x2, 2000 Speight, 2006 Bainimarama), ethnic tensions (indigenous vs Indo-Fijian), 2013 constitution, return to democracy.

religion.note: Christianity dominant among iTaukei (Methodist ~35%, Catholic, Assemblies of God; Methodism introduced 1835, deeply embedded in indigenous culture/chiefly system); Hinduism (Indo-Fijian community, girmitiya descendants, temples); Islam (Gujarati/Indo-Fijian); Sunday sabbath strictly observed (shops close, no sport); religion ethnically aligned (indigenous=Christian, Indian=Hindu/Muslim); church central to village life

ethnic_groups.name: iTaukei (Indigenous Fijian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Melanesian/Polynesian; mataqali (clan) land ownership (83% land communally owned by iTaukei, cannot be sold, only leased, central political issue); chiefly system (Ratu/Adi titles, Great Council of Chiefs dissolved 2012 restored 2023); kava (yaqona) ceremony central; meke dance; 'vanua' (land/people/custom interconnected); rugby (national passion, 7s Olympic gold 2016/2020); politically dominant; feared losing power to Indo-Fijians (drove coups)

ethnic_groups.name: Indo-Fijian
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of indentured labourers (girmitiya, 'agreement' Hindi, brought by British 1879-1916, ~60k total, sugar plantations); declined from 51% in 1966 to 37% (emigration after coups 1987/2000, brain drain to Australia/NZ/Canada); Fiji Hindi (pidgin, not standard Hindi); commercially dominant (shopkeepers, professionals); land tenure insecure (cannot own native land, leases expire); political marginalisation; 1987/2000 coups targeted Indo-Fijians; Sitiveni Rabuka's ethno-nationalist coups 1987; resilient community

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Rotuman (~10k, Polynesian, Rotuma island, distinct culture/language, autonomy); Chinese (~6k, business community); European (~3k, colonial legacy); Part-European; Banaban (resettled from Kiribati, Rabi Island, phosphate refugees); Solomon Islander; Tongan

country_profile.notes_unique: Four coups in 20 years (1987 Rabuka x2, 2000 Speight civilian, 2006 Bainimarama military; ethnic tensions iTaukei vs Indo-Fijian drove all; unique 'coup culture'); girmitiya legacy (1879-1916, British brought ~60k indentured Indian labourers, 'agreement'/girmit, sugar plantations, descendants now 37%, parallel society, Fiji Hindi language emerged); land system (83% iTaukei communal ownership, mataqali, cannot be sold, Indo-Fijians cannot own native land, leases contentious, drives emigration); rugby sevens (national obsession, 2016 Rio Olympic gold Fiji's first Olympic medal, national holiday declared, 2020 Tokyo retained); Fiji water (exported globally, ironic given local water access issues); 332 islands (110 inhabited); coral reefs (Great Astrolabe Reef); Cannibal Isles (historical reputation, Ratu Udre Udre allegedly ate 872 people, last recorded 1867); firewalking (Beqa Island, Sawau tribe); bula greeting; kava culture; climate change existential threat (sea level rise, cyclones intensifying, Cyclone Winston 2016 Category 5 strongest in Southern Hemisphere); sugar industry (declining, Indo-Fijian farmers, land lease expiry crisis)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Sitiveni Rabuka
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: People's Alliance / PAP coalition; military officer who led 1987 coups (twice!); imprisoned then forgiven; returned to politics; won 2022 narrowly in coalition with NFP (multiracial party); ironic: coup-maker now democratic PM for second time (first time 1992-99); reconciliation rhetoric; iTaukei champion

head_of_state.name: Ratu Wiliame Katonivere
head_of_state.title: President
head_of_state.notes: Ceremonial; Paramount Chief of Macuata; appointed by Parliament; iTaukei; replaced Konrote

former_leaders.name: Frank Bainimarama
former_leaders.notes: Military coup 2006 (ousted Qarase); ruled by decree 2006-14; 2013 constitution (removed race from law, equal citizenship); won elections 2014/2018 (FijiFirst party); climate champion internationally; authoritarian domestically; lost 2022 election narrowly; arrested 2023 (sedition charges); imprisoned; pardoned 2024; fell from grace

former_leaders.name: Laisenia Qarase
former_leaders.notes: SDL; interim PM after 2000 Speight coup; elected 2001/2006; pro-iTaukei affirmative action (controversial); ousted by Bainimarama 2006 coup; convicted of corruption 2012

former_leaders.name: Mahendra Chaudhry
former_leaders.notes: FLP (Fiji Labour Party); first Indo-Fijian PM (historic); held hostage 56 days during Speight's 2000 coup; symbolised Indo-Fijian political arrival; ethnic backlash

former_leaders.name: Sitiveni Rabuka (1st time)
former_leaders.notes: SVT; led 1987 coups but won democratic elections; 1997 constitution (replaced racist 1990 version); lost 1999 to Chaudhry; later apologised for coups; military-to-democrat arc

former_leaders.name: Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara
former_leaders.notes: Alliance Party; founding father; led independence 1970; Paramount Chief Lau; balanced ethnic politics; PM 22 years; President from 1993; displaced in 2000 coup; died 2004; 'Father of the Nation'
